newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila destroys "Chinese structures" in Spratlys.
newsitem.headline: Manila destroys "Chinese structures" in Spratlys.

text.p: The Philippines has destroyed new structures it believes China built near areas claimed by Manila on the disputed Spratly Islands, military officials said on Monday.

Defence Secretary Renato de Villa has briefed the cabinet on the military operation, carried out earlier this month to remove concrete slabs and cylindrical buoys, said the officials, who asked not to be named.
The structures were found on a rocky outcrop called Sabina Shoal, 120 km (75 miles) west of the southwestern Philippine island of Palawan.
"Who else could have put them there but them (the Chinese)?" a senior officer said.
The Spratlys are a cluster of islands, reefs and atolls in the South China Sea which are believed to sit atop huge oil and gas reserves and which Beijing says historically belongs to China.
The area is also claimed totally or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, Malaysia and Brunei, as well as the Philippines.
In 1995, the Philippines removed or destroyed several markers or floating buoys which Manila said the Chinese set up at six reefs and shoals near islands it claims in the Spratlys.
Chinese-Philippine relations have been strained by competing claims over the islands.

In April, Manila accused Beijing of sending naval vessels near two islands occupied by Filipinos. Beijing in turn accused Manila of violating China's sovereignty after Filipinos flew their flag over a cluster of rocks called Scarborough Shoal north of the Spratlys.
Last month the Philippines arrested 21 Chinese fishermen near Scarborough and charged them with illegal entry after rejecting China's demand for their release.
